facts.text: Open-loop replay of recorded sensor data uses the real production software and optionally the original sensor-processing ECU.
facts.quote: **What is real:** the production software and, optionally, the original sensor-processing ECU.

facts.text: Open-loop replay needs raw or near-raw sensor streams: camera frames before lossy compression, radar detections or ideally ADC or radar-cube data, lidar point clouds, and ultrasonic echo data.
facts.quote: raw or near-raw sensor streams (camera frames before lossy compression, radar detections or ideally ADC or radar-cube data, lidar point clouds, ultrasonic echo data)

facts.text: Open-loop replay needs machine-state buses, exact original timing and time synchronisation, calibration and configuration, and independent ground truth or an expected output for scoring.
facts.quote: machine-state buses, exact original timing and time synchronisation, calibration and configuration, and an independent ground truth or expected output to score against.

facts.text: Commercial automotive replay documentation stresses original data interfaces, synchronisation and timing.
facts.quote: Commercial replay documentation stresses original data interfaces, synchronisation and timing. **Vendor (on-road evidence)** [11].

facts.text: Open-loop replay can establish detection rate, false-alarm rate and warning timing for the recorded sensor configuration in the recorded situations.
facts.quote: **Proves:** detection rate, false-alarm rate and warning timing of the recorded sensor configuration in the recorded situations

facts.text: Open-loop replay can establish repeatability.
facts.quote: repeatability

facts.text: Open-loop replay can establish software and perception regression across versions.
facts.quote: software and perception regression across versions

facts.text: Open-loop replay can establish the old-system baseline and is the natural method for baselining the existing system.
facts.quote: the old-system baseline; and an old-versus-new comparison when both systems accept genuinely equivalent inputs. It is the natural method for baselining the existing system.

facts.text: Open-loop replay can support an old-versus-new system comparison when both systems accept genuinely equivalent inputs.
facts.quote: an old-versus-new comparison when both systems accept genuinely equivalent inputs.

facts.text: Open-loop replay cannot prove the effect of an action, such as braking, steering or an operator reaction, that differs from the recording.
facts.quote: **Cannot prove:** the effect of any action, such as braking, steering or an operator reaction that differs from the recording

facts.text: Open-loop replay cannot prove anything about sensor types or positions that were not recorded.
facts.quote: anything about sensor types or positions that were not recorded

facts.text: Open-loop replay cannot prove performance under new environmental conditions or failures absent from the logs.
facts.quote: new environmental conditions or failures that are not in the logs

facts.text: Open-loop replay cannot prove physical sensor effects when re-injection occurs downstream of the sensor.
facts.quote: physical sensor effects when re-injection happens downstream of the sensor.

facts.text: Open-loop replay is standard practice in automotive development.
facts.quote: **Evidence:** standard practice in automotive development.

facts.text: Li et al. documented the open-loop failure mode for systems that act in CVPR 2024.
facts.quote: The open-loop failure mode for systems that act is documented by Li et al. (CVPR 2024). **Independent (on-road evidence)** [18].

facts.text: Vendor implementation evidence for replay is mature in automotive development.
facts.quote: Vendor implementation evidence is mature in automotive

facts.text: Direct heavy off-road replay evidence is sparse.
facts.quote: direct heavy off-road replay evidence is sparse.

facts.text: Replay fidelity is defined by the injection boundary.
facts.quote: **replay fidelity is defined by the injection boundary**

facts.text: If an old camera produces a serialized image stream over a GMSL link and those frames are recorded, re-injecting the frames into the image ECU tests everything downstream of that injection point.
facts.quote: Suppose the old camera produces a serialized image stream over a GMSL link and the recording captures those frames. Re-injecting them into the image ECU tests everything downstream of that point

facts.text: Re-injecting recorded camera frames into the image ECU does not retest the old lens, exposure control, imager, lens contamination, vibration or sun-glare response.
facts.quote: it does not retest the old lens, exposure control, imager, lens contamination, vibration or sun-glare response.

facts.text: Putting the real camera back in the replay loop with a monitor, called a camera box, includes the optics again.
facts.quote: Putting the real camera back in the loop with a monitor ("camera box") includes the optics again

facts.text: Camera-box replay is limited by monitor contrast, optics and multi-camera geometry.
facts.quote: monitor contrast, optics and multi-camera geometry then become test limitations.

facts.text: dSPACE describes camera-box limitations and downstream raw-image injection in automotive vendor documentation.
facts.quote: dSPACE describes both the camera-box limitations and downstream raw-image injection. **Vendor (on-road evidence)** [12].
